title: The mod-test typecheck arm is inert in CI (NOT TYPECHECKED), and four pre-existing tests/board.test.tsx errors wait behind it
description:
Found 2026-10-03 while shipping the seq 213 wording fixes on #486 (commit 69c698a4), running the mod gate on this machine after the session loaded the plugin-authoring skill, which lays a Claude Code 2.1.288 declaration that scripts/mod-test.mjs picks up. Reported to opum-agent; filed here on its instruction, deliberately not fixed on #486, whose scope was exactly the two wording fixes.

(a) Four pre-existing type errors in tests/board.test.tsx, revealed the moment the runner typechecks: two ui.render AbovePrompt mocks returning h(...) where RenderElement is required (RenderNode|null|undefined flows through), at 69c698a4 lines 1087 and 1146 (pre-change 1062 and 1116); and two AlertDecision waiting fixtures missing the required status, at 69c698a4 lines 1744 and 1745 (pre-change 1714 and 1715). Control evidence: with the seq 213 change stashed, the identical four errors appear at the pre-change lines, so none of them is introduced by 69c698a4.

(b) The gate gap: scripts/mod-test.mjs typechecks only against a declaration whose header names the RUNNING Claude Code. CI (source-gates) installs @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.287 globally and lays no declaration, so its arm reports NOT TYPECHECKED and the gate is green by absence -- green at both 0ae361d3 and 69c698a4 -- while fleet sessions run 2.1.288, where the arm is live and fails on (a). The arm exists precisely to gate (QCLI-431 design); today it never does in CI.

Not blocking the held pair release as configured. opum-agent carries this id into the paired-release prep list for opum-doc to decide whether it folds in before the re-freeze.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The four pre-existing tests/board.test.tsx type errors are fixed, and the mod runner typecheck arm reports clean against the declaration naming the running Claude Code: the closing line names that declaration and the run exits 0.

The CI gap is closed or ruled: either a source-gates run typechecks the mod -- its closing line names the declaration it checked against and the run is green -- or the task record cites the decision that the arm stays local-only by design, with the NOT TYPECHECKED state deliberately accepted.
